terrain_atlas.sprite_art: authored NES icons; original actor identities and positions retained

method: Compare bounded SLZ output byte for byte with the official decompressed globe and belt source files. Compare all four original projection LUTs byte for byte.

Independently interpret original globe coordinates, map offsets and sprite-shape offsets over all 256 camera views and 64 source sprites per view. Preserve source record order and measure the nearest-8-pixel coordinate error on each axis.

Independently reconstruct all 32 water/fire/conveyor animation phases from the original source buffer layout and phase formulas. Unpack original 4bpp pixels separately, apply the declared three-color reduction and compare each mapped pattern with the final resident NES CHR.
Count alpha-mask changes separately from bit-plane changes. These describe the visual approximation; they do not affect the shared logical collision map.
limits: Static asset recovery and adapted-projection metrics, not native NES rendering or whole-game parity.
The shared 214-pattern terrain atlas is lossy. Original palette hues are reduced and some transparency pixels change.
Quantized sprite rectangles overlap; a background renderer must define depth and transparency composition. This receipt checks source record order and coordinates, not final occlusion correctness.
Original art, ROM, LUT bytes and converted CHR remain private and are absent from this artifact.
post_recovery_sprite_adapter: Distinct authored icons plus nearest2x16pxplayer and16pxraftdeck. Player quad row-major/scaling checked against the original authored8pxglyph; native visibility is a separate cartridge gate.
